class.name: NNSTNode
class.brief_description: Runs business logic for a state tree.
class.description:
This is the workhorse of the State Tree. It acts as all the other levels of the state tree other than the tree root. If a [NNSTNode] has no child nodes, it is considered a leaf node. If it has child nodes, it is considered like a selector in a behaviour tree: it will evaluate its child nodes to find a leaf node to activate. To make use of the [NNSTNode], override the following virtual methods in each state's script: [gdscript] extends NNSTNode
func on_enter_condition() -> bool: # Do your logic here to decide when this node should be activated. # Return true or false based on your logic. return true
func on_enter_state() -> void: # Initialize your state here. pass
func on_exit_state() -> void: # Clean up before exiting the state here. pass
func on_tick(delta: float) -> void: # Do what ever the state needs to do here. pass [/gdscript]

members.member: Optional path to a direct child state or [NNSTHistory] node. Non-direct-child paths are cleared to empty on assignment. When pointing at a state, that child is evaluated first when choosing a child to enter, followed by the remaining children in tree order. When pointing at an [NNSTHistory], this state restores the history's remembered or default state instead of running normal child selection (falling back to normal child selection if nothing can be restored).
